item.text:
### (a) Social posts

1. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, it will drive hundreds of deep-sea species extinct. We cannot allow mining companies to destroy ancient habitats before we even understand them. The deep ocean is alive—and we must protect it.

2. We reject the idea that the deep sea is an industrial zone. It is a living ecosystem filled with rare and remarkable species. Commercial mining will drive hundreds of them extinct. We must stop it before it starts.

3. Deep-sea mining means machines tearing through ancient habitats, burying marine life in sediment and causing irreversible destruction. We know where this leads: hundreds of species driven extinct. We demand protection, not extraction.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 101 words

The deep ocean is not an empty frontier. It is home to extraordinary species found nowhere else, many of which science is only beginning to understand. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, it will drive hundreds of those species extinct. We refuse to accept irreversible destruction as the price of minerals ripped from the seabed. Mining machines would tear through ancient habitats, bury marine life in sediment and unleash damage that cannot be undone. We are calling for a halt before extraction starts, and for leaders to protect the deep sea as a living ecosystem, not sacrifice it as an industrial zone.
